text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe has lost an estimated Z$3 billion in potential investment in the past three years after investors, frustrated by red tape at Harare's companies' registry office, took their projects elsewhere, legal and financial experts say.

- A committee negotiating improved pay and service conditions for civil servants on Wednesday accused the government of not honouring its committment to bargain with workers in good faith, warning it would not be held responsible for any action the workers might decide to take.

- America's former top African expert Chester Crocker on Wednesday took a swipe at the Zimbabwe government's decision to award a Z$6 billion contract to a Malaysian firm for the expansion of Hwange Thermal Power plant without going through an open tender system.

- An International Monetary Fund (IMF) team is due in Zimbabwe next week to study the second phase of its economic reform programme and find out whether the southern African country has achieved fiscal integrity before committing the IMF to supporting the programme.
- TA Holdings has unveiled a major streamlining and perfomance improvement strategy that will see the company's profits and turnover grow and become more competitive.

- Foreign investors will have an opportunity to participate in Zimbabwe's privatisation programme, but will be persuaded to go into joint ventures with local black entrepreneurs, president Robert Mugabe said at the opening of a two-day Southern Africa Trade and Investment Summit in Harare on Wednesday.
